name: Delhi Darwaza Guide
title: Sample heritage guide
notes: Sample content for the demo. Shaniwar Wada was the seat of the Peshwas, begun around 1730. The Delhi Darwaza is its main northern gate, named because it faces north towards Delhi. It is tall enough for an elephant carrying a rider, and the heavy doors are said to be studded with spikes to resist elephant charges. A fire in 1828 destroyed the timber palace, but the stone walls and gates survive. Tip: come early in the morning when the plaza is quiet and the light hits the gate. Say clearly when a date or detail is uncertain.

name: Courtyard Storyteller
title: Sample local historian
notes: Sample content for the demo. The Peshwa residence at Shaniwar Wada was begun around 1730 and occupied in 1732. Today the stone plinth survives while the upper floors were largely timber and brick. Traditional accounts say the palace rose several storeys, up to seven, but treat that number as tradition. A major fire in 1828 destroyed the palace interior; the cause is not certain. Tip: wear comfortable shoes, the ground is uneven.

name: Colosseum Corner Guide
title: Sample local guide
notes: Sample content for the demo. The Colosseum is a large amphitheatre in the centre of Rome, built of travertine, tuff and brick in the first century AD. It hosted public spectacles. Practical tips from a sample local: the queue at the main entrance is longest from mid-morning, so buy tickets in advance and come at opening time or late afternoon; the metro stop named after the monument is the easiest way in; there is a free public fountain with drinkable water nearby. The arches on the outer ring are numbered, which helped crowds find their seats.

name: Trastevere Evening Guide
title: Sample food lover
place_name: Piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere
notes: Sample content for the demo. Trastevere is a neighbourhood on the west bank of the Tiber with narrow cobbled lanes. The piazza in front of the basilica is the social centre in the evening. Sample local tips: the best time to wander is just before dinner, around 6 pm; restaurants right on the main piazza are pricier, side streets are better value; try cacio e pepe, a Roman pasta with pecorino and black pepper; the lanes are slippery when wet.

name: Eiffel Tower Lawn Guide
title: Sample photographer
place_name: Champ de Mars, near the Eiffel Tower
notes: Sample content for the demo. The Eiffel Tower is an iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, completed in 1889. Sample local photography tips: the classic wide shot works from the lawn of the Champ de Mars; the Trocadero terrace across the river gives the full view at sunrise with few people; the tower sparkles for a few minutes at the start of each hour after dark. Pickpockets target crowded queues, keep bags closed.

name: Montmartre Steps Guide
title: Sample art walker
notes: Sample content for the demo. Montmartre is a hill in the north of Paris, topped by the white basilica of Sacre-Coeur. Many painters worked here in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. Sample local tips: the funicular is the easy way up but the stairs give better views; the small square with portrait artists is crowded in the afternoon, early morning is peaceful; people offering friendship bracelets on the steps can be politely declined.

name: Times Square Survivor Guide
title: Sample city local
notes: Sample content for the demo. Times Square is the bright pedestrian crossroads of Broadway and Seventh Avenue in Manhattan. Sample local tips: it is loudest and most crowded on evenings and weekends; the discounted ticket booth for same-day theatre tickets sits at the north end; costumed characters ask for tips after photos, you can simply decline; the cleanest restrooms are in nearby hotel lobbies and public library branches. Walk one block west for quieter restaurants.

name: Central Park Bridge Guide
title: Sample runner
notes: Sample content for the demo. Bow Bridge is a cast-iron footbridge over the lake in Central Park, Manhattan. Sample local tips: it is most photographed in autumn and at golden hour; arrive before 8 am on weekends to get it nearly to yourself; rowboats can be rented at the nearby boathouse in warm months; the loop road around the park is shared with cyclists, so stay on the walking path.

name: Senso-ji Morning Guide
title: Sample temple visitor
notes: Sample content for the demo. Senso-ji is a Buddhist temple in Asakusa, Tokyo, entered through the large Kaminarimon gate with a big red lantern. A long shopping street called Nakamise leads to the main hall. Sample local tips: arrive before 8 am to avoid crowds; it is customary to rinse your hands at the fountain before approaching the hall; you can draw an omikuji fortune slip for a small fee; eating while walking on the shopping street is frowned upon, stand beside the stall instead.

name: Big Ben Riverside Guide
title: Sample commuter
notes: Sample content for the demo. The clock tower at the Palace of Westminster, popularly called Big Ben, stands beside Westminster Bridge on the River Thames in London. Sample local tips: the best view of the tower is from the middle of the bridge or the south bank path; the bridge is very crowded at midday; the bells chime on the hour; the south bank walk towards the big wheel is flat and pleasant, with street food stalls; use the tube stop named Westminster, and mind the gap on the platform.
